headline: Memory chipmakers are putting more than NT$674 billion (about US$21 billion) into new production in Taiwan because AI demand has created a memory shortage.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a concrete investment total with named sites and dates, but it is a compilation of company plans relayed from CNA.
importance_line: New factories could eventually ease the memory squeeze for PC, phone and server makers, but most of the new capacity arrives only from late 2027 to 2029, and the dates are company plans.
summary: Taiwan's Central News Agency (CNA) reports, as carried by Taiwan News, that Micron, Nanya, Winbond and Macronix are expanding memory production in Taiwan as AI-driven demand creates a memory shortage and lifts prices. Micron is adding capacity at four sites, with a second advanced packaging plant in Taichung due to start mass production in mid-October, Nanya plans to open its Fab 5A in the second half of 2027 and reach 35,900 wafer starts a month by 2029, and Winbond targets mass production at an expanded Kaohsiung site at the end of 2029.
notes: Article credits CNA for the details; CNA original not read. The page text also mentions an NT$85.1 billion Micron figure whose scope is unclear, so it was left out.
